brief: Holds a hexadecimal number and writes it in decimal, binary, octal or any base up to 36.
detail: Built from text with or without a prefix (FF, 0xFF, U+0041); the digits are kept without the prefix and WithPrefix adds 0x back. The conversions go through a floating-point number, so they are exact up to 9007199254740992 and rounded above. The From... methods replace the number in place from a decimal, octal or binary value. Checked by hand: 0xFF is 255, 0b11111111 and 0o377; 0x1A3 is 419, 0b110100011 and 0o643; 0xDEADBEEF is 3735928559. Found today: FractionalPart and ToScientificForm raise R14; IntegerPartWithoutPrefix keeps a stray 0 (0xFF gives 0FF); ToUnicodeHexForm keeps the 0x inside the U+ (U+0x41); and FromDecimalForm stores -1 and FF. for a negative and a fraction.
